Testimony LD 491 - Resolve, Authorizing ACF to Convey and Release State's interest in Certain Real Property Located in the Town of Richmond
Public Hearing Date: February 27, 2025, Thursday, at 1pm
Senator Talbot-Ross, Representative Plueker, and members of the Agriculture, Conservation, and
Forestry committee, good afternoon, my name is Heather O. Popadak. I am testifying in favor of
LD 491, "Resotve, Authorizing the Department ofAgriculture, Conservation and Forestry to Convey and Release the State's Interest in Certain Real Property Located in the Town of
Richmond", at the request of my 87-year-old mother, Wilhelmine "Billie" Oakes.
In the interest of transparency, I work for the State of Maine, and I am taking personal time off to
attend this public hearing.
it may be helpfulto hearthe back story surroundingthis parcel in the Town of Richmond and why
this parcel is in front of the Legislature again.
On two separate occasions, decades apart, the Town of Richmond sold and transferred a parcel of land owned by the State. The current transferee of that parcel, Wilhelmine Oakes, is seeking
to clear the parcel's title and obtain a release of the State's interest.
The State's interest in the parcel began in 1960, when the prior owner died intestate. With no known heirs, the decedent's parcel escheated to the State.
in 1965, the Town of Richmond sold the parcel to mother and daughter, Elosowet and Rosalia Slostowsky, "by virtue of unpaid taxes for the tax years 1961, 1962, 1963, 1964, 1965." (Sagadahoc County Registry of Deeds, Book 332, Page 563). However, there were no recorded or matured tax liens on the parcel for those tax years; the parcel had escheated to the State in
1960.
From 1967 to 1996, almost 30 years, various letters were exchanged among the parcel's
interested parties and brought to the attention of the Town in the 1970s. But the Town took no action following this information and eventually, the matter was addressed legislatively.

Testimony LD 491 - Resolve, Authorizing ACF to Convey and Release State's interest in Certain Real Property Located in the Town of Richmond
Public Hearing Date: February 27, 2025, Thursday, at 1 pm
In April 1996, the State authorized the sale of the State's interest in the parcel to Rosalia. it is not
known why, but actions to finalize clearing the title were not completed. By this time, Elesowet (1985) and her husband, Marian (1992), were deceased.
In 1999, three years after the State authorized the sale of the parcel, the Town filed a tax lien
against the property for failure to pay taxes.
In June 2000, Rosalia released the parcel back to the Town of Richmond. All unpaid taxes on the parcel were abated by the Town in early 2002.
in April 2006, the Town deeded the parcel to Mrs. Oakes' predecessor-in-title. In 2008, this individual deeded the parcel to Mrs. Oakes. Mrs. Oakes became aware of the parcel's title defects and attempted to resolve the issue with the Town in 2019. Her efforts, however, were
unsuccessful.
Attempts to resolve the issue with the Town of Richmond have been unsuccessful and Mrs. Oakes is seeking legislative relief to clear this title. LD 491 would provide this relief. I urge this committee to vote `Ought to Pass' on LD 491 to resolve this matter.
Thankyou for yourtime and I am happy to answeryour questions.

Testimony of Rep. Sally Cluchey presenting
LD 491 Resolve, Authorizing the Department ofAgriculture, Conservation and Forestry to Convey
and Release the State 's Interest in Certain Real Property Located in the Town ofRichmond Before the Joint Standing Committee on Agriculture Conservation and Forestry
Good afternoon, Senator Talbot-Ross, Representative Pluecker, and members of the Agriculture,
Conservation, and Forestry Committee. My name is Sally Cluchey, and I represent House District 52, which includes Bowdoinham, Bowdoin, and Richmond. I am here today to present LD 491, a resolve
authorizing the Department of Agriculture, Conservation, and Forestry to release the State's interest in a parcel of land in Richmond.
This bill seeks to resolve a long-standing title issue affecting 87-year-old Wilhelmine D. Oakes. Decades
ago, the Town of Richmond mistakenly sold a parcel of land that had escheated to the State in 1960 after the previous owner died intestate with no known heirs. The Town sold the parcel twice-~f1rst in 1965
and again in 2006. Mrs. Oakes acquired the property in 2008 and has been trying to clear the title since
2019.
Although a legislative attempt was Inade to resolve this issue in 1996, the transfer was never completed.
Efforts to address it with the Town of Richmond have been unsuccessful, leaving Mrs. Oakes with no
option but to seek legislative relief. LD 491 would formally release the State's interest and allow her to
clear the title.
I have spoken with the Town and Director Cutko of the Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands, and it is my
understanding that all parties support resolving this matter. Mrs. Oakes is here today, and her daughter is available to provide further details and answer any questions.
Thank you for your time and consideration.
